text: Foundations introduced owners, stewards, councils, and sponsors one at a time. This lesson puts them in one picture, and covers how you actually get a real person productive in one of these roles — closing out the chapter on launching the program.

A RACI matrix answers who does what for every activity at once. Responsible does the work. Accountable owns the outcome and signs off. Consulted gives input beforehand. Informed is told after. The discipline that matters: every single activity gets exactly one Accountable.

The most common mistake is assigning Accountable to more than one role, or to none, because it feels collaborative. It's the opposite. When an issue sits unresolved for weeks, "everyone's a little responsible" means nobody actually is, and it has nowhere specific to land.

Defining a role on paper and getting someone productive in it are different problems. A practical sequence: a written role description tied to the RACI matrix, context on the charter's scope and the "why," the actual tools and access, a shadow period with the previous holder, and a formal, visible announcement.
Chapter one is complete — charter, stakeholders, councils, stewardship, and roles. Chapter two moves into the actual output of all this structure: writing governance policies.
